purpose: Product-intent confirmation record. For each link the owner supplied, this file stores the product the owner INTENDED to promote, and separately the product the link was OBSERVED to resolve to. The two are never merged: an intent is not evidence, and an observation is not consent. A row is 'confirmed' only when a human has seen the same product at both ends and recorded the date.
why_two_fields: Amazon defines an ASIN as the unique 10-character identifier of a listing, which makes the intended product checkable rather than remembered. Merging 'what I meant to link' with 'what the link opened' would let an observation silently overwrite an intent, and the record would then assert a match that nobody checked.
rules: intended_asin, intended_listing_url and intended_source are transcribed from the owner's brief and are not evidence of anything working.
observed_redirect_target and observed_listing_title are what a fetch actually returned, with the date, and are not evidence of what the owner wanted.
confirmation_date stays null until the owner confirms the match from a logged-in browser. No session may fill it on the owner's behalf.
a blank field means unknown. It is never inferred from a neighbouring field.
observation_method: Server-side fetch of each supplied link.amazon URL with redirects followed. The final URL, its /dp/<ASIN> path and the page <title> were recorded. Landing on a fallback-style URL (lv=shuf, plpRedirect=mhFallback) does not by itself prove the ASIN is a live buyable listing, so the title is recorded alongside it.

associates_tag.format_rule: Amazon Program Policies §2(b) publishes the tag format as XXXXX-##.
associates_tag.note: The tag is this site's own Associates ID. It was appended to the site's outbound links by this pass. Its ABSENCE from the five supplied link.amazon URLs is recorded per row below; that absence is what makes those URLs not Special Links as supplied.
